answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring every agent to lock a refundable stake before it can transact, like a marble token held in escrow: one identity costs one stake, so spawning an ocean of sock-puppets multiplies the attacker's locked capital instead of being free. Peers verify the stake on-chain, and any identity caught double-signing or spamming loses its stake, so the ripple of one bad actor's punishment deters the rest. Honest agents get their stake back, while a Sybil farmer must pay for every fake.
